newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.

text.p: In the South, rice prices were steady. Long grain milled rice prices were selling mostly at $19.50 to $20.00 per cwt, medium grain traded mostly at $18.50 to $19.00, second heads were steady to 0.50 cents higher at $14.00 to $15.00, and brewers remain in very tight supply with few sales at $14.75. Rice by-products were near steady.
In California, rice prices were steady with medium grain selling mostly at $19.50 to $20.00. Rice bran was uneven, near steady.

California rice ship loadings: At the Port of Sacramento for the week ending November 16, 1996: there were no rice ship loadings. Inspections of California rice for export: There were no inspections of milled rice for the week ending November 16, 1996.
The yearly total since October 1, 1996 is 303,270 cwt compared to 853,458 cwt a year ago.

The following prices were for domestic shipment -- offers, FOB mills, milled rice, dollars per cwt, bagged. (All milled rice grade 2 not to exceed 4 percent brokens, except California grade 1. All second heads grade 4 or better)
Feed by-products prices (dollars per short ton, fob mills).
